study.title: Sensorimotor Responses in Post-Stroke Hemiplegic Patients Modulated by Acupuncture at Yanglingquan (GB34): A fMRI Study Using Intersubject Functional Correlation (ISFC) Analysis
study.study_design: Single-center cross-sectional fMRI study with within-subject multiple scan conditions (resting state, motor task, acupuncture task) in two groups (post-stroke inpatient patients and healthy controls)
study.population: Right-handed post-stroke inpatient subjects with hemiplegia and age- and sex-matched healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients: (1) ischemic stroke conforming to diagnostic criteria, course within 3 months; (2) right-handed; (3) aged 40-75 years; (4) first-ever post-stroke motor dysfunction in upper or lower extremities; (5) infarction located in basal ganglia and/or corona radiate region, side-unlimited, but not caused by embolism; (6) without other central nervous system diseases (e.g., epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia), psychiatric disorders (e.g., depression and schizophrenia), or serious primary diseases (e.g., tumors, organ failure, atrial fibrillation, thrombotic diseases); (7) without unremovable metallic implants or contraindication of magnetic resonance examination. Controls: (1) right-handed; (2) aged 40-75 years; (3) proved healthy by medical examination (without organic or significant functional diseases); (4) without family history of mental or neural system inheritance; (5) without experience of joining similar research; (6) without physical abnormalities (e.g., cold, headache, cough) during the trial; (7) not taking excitatory medications within past 2 months; (8) without unremovable metallic implants or contraindication of magnetic resonance examination.
study.exclusion_criteria: Implied by inclusion criteria; not separately stated as exclusion criteria list

conditions.scan_context: 6 min 10 s resting-state fMRI; participants told to close eyes without engaging in any mental task
Passive thumb-index-finger opposition on affected side (patients) or left side (controls); rest-move-rest-move-rest-move-rest pattern; each time slice 20 s; total 2 min 20 s; move period at 1 Hz

Acupuncture at GB34 on affected side (patients) or left side (controls); 10-s post-onset resting phase with needle inserted, followed by 1-min manual stimulation, then 8-min post-stimulation phase with needle remaining

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: On the outside of the lower leg, in the middle of the concavity of the anterior and inferior parts of the fibula head
interventions.depth_exact: 1.5–2 Cun (about 25–40 mm depending on the height and weight of a participant)
interventions.manipulation_exact: Mild reinforcing–reducing method at a frequency of 1 Hz for 1 min
interventions.needle_retention_exact: Needle remaining inside the leg during 8-min post-stimulation phase; removed and disposed of after acupuncture scanning
interventions.session_duration_exact: 10 s post-onset resting phase + 1 min manual stimulation + 8 min post-stimulation phase
interventions.treatment_period_exact: Single session on day of scanning
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Close eyes without engaging in any mental task; kept awake during whole scanning procedure
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: GB34 is the He-Sea point of the gall bladder meridian (Foot-Shaoyang), the confluence point of tendons; one of the main points in post-stroke acupuncture approaches; most commonly used acupoint to study mechanism of acupuncture stimulation in stroke based on fMRI

sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Sensory/deqi responses were not formally measured or reported in this study. Participants were told to close eyes and not engage in mental tasks. Participants confirmed remaining awake after scanning. No deqi instrument was used.

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: echo-planar imaging (EPI) sequence for fMRI; T1W1 sequence for structural
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: not_reported (matrix 64 × 64; FOV 225 × 225 mm; slice thickness 3.5 mm; gap 0.7 mm)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Resting state: 6 min 10 s; Motor task: 2 min 20 s; Acupuncture task: ~9 min 10 s (10 s + 1 min + 8 min); T1: 5 min 10 s
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: fMRIPrep; 3dTshift from AFNI (RRID:SCR_005927); mcflirt (FSL 5.0.11); bbregister (FreeSurfer); ICA-AROMA
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: Brain Imaging Analysis Kit (BrainIAK, https://brainiak.org) implemented in Python
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: isotropic Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Head-motion parameters estimated using mcflirt; Framewise displacement (FD), DVARS calculated; ICA-AROMA for automatic removal of motion artifacts
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: 3 region-wise global signals within cerebrospinal fluid, white matter, and whole-brain masks calculated; component-based noise correction performed
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: False discovery rate (FDR) correction; bootstrap hypothesis test with confidence intervals 95%, random state 1,000, resampling iterations 1,000; Monte Carlo approximate permutation tests for group comparisons

extraction_notes.note: No sham/control acupuncture arm was included. The study compared real acupuncture at GB34 vs. motor task within the same participants, and vs. healthy controls. No sham needling or placebo procedure was used.
Deqi/sensory responses to acupuncture were not formally measured or reported. The paper provides no sensory rating instrument (e.g., MASS, VAS) data.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events were not reported in the paper.
No trial registration number was reported.

Specific ROI pairs in subgroup comparisons (C1 vs. C2 in Figure 7I; Nih1 vs. Nih3 in Figure 8I; Nih2 vs. Nih3 in Figure 8J) are shown in figures but the individual ROI pairs are not enumerated in the text. Edge-level extraction for these contrasts is incomplete due to figure-only reporting.

ISFC matrix figures (Figures 4-8) show color-coded connectivity values but exact numeric ISFC values and specific significant pairs for many contrasts are not reported in text tables. Only selected significant pairs are described in the Results section text.

The paper refers to 'ipsilesional' hemisphere as right (R) for all patients, after flipping left-hemisphere lesion patients' data. ROI labels with _R refer to the affected (ipsilesional) hemisphere and _L to the contralesional hemisphere for the patient group, contrary to the standard anatomical convention where L=left, R=right.

Scan duration for the acupuncture task is described as 10 s needle insertion + 1 min stimulation + 8 min post-stimulation, totaling approximately 9 min 10 s, but the exact number of volumes/TRs acquired is not reported.

The paper states that in the acupuncture task, a '1-min manual stimulation phase by using the mild reinforcing-reducing method at a frequency of 1 Hz' was applied, but does not specify whether deqi was achieved or sought.

Exact MNI coordinates are not reported anywhere in the paper for any result. The analysis is ROI-based using the Brainnetome atlas, and results are reported as named ROI regions or connectivity pairs, not as peak coordinates.
Supplementary Material 1 is referenced for additional preprocessing details but is not included in the provided PDF. Specific filtering and preprocessing steps may be more fully described there.

For subgroup C1 ISC results, the text lists six activated ROIs (A4ul_R, A4tl_R, A4tl_L, A2_L, A6m_L, A1/2/3tru_R). It is stated these are ISC activations, but the paper also describes ISFC pairs for this subgroup simultaneously. The boundary between ISC and ISFC results is clear from reading but extracted separately here as they are distinct analyses.

Motor task scan was only 2 min 20 s, which is short for typical fMRI analyses. The acupuncture scan was approximately 9 min 10 s. Differences in scan duration may influence ISC/ISFC estimates but this is not discussed in the paper.

Table 3 lists subgroup Nih1 with NIHSS 0.44 ± 0.51 (range 0-1), Nih2 with NIHSS 2.9 ± 0.77 (range 2-4), Nih3 with NIHSS 7.13 ± 2.37 (range 5-15). The sum of subgroup sample sizes (18+21+24=63) matches the total patient group, indicating no overlap or exclusion.

The paper does not use a GLM or HRF model. ISFC is data-driven and based on inter-subject temporal correlations. The acupuncture 'task' ISFC results reflect shared neural fluctuations across subjects during the scan, not necessarily direct acupuncture-evoked activation in the traditional sense.
